# T3 direct dispatch and thread reads recorded 2026-11-21, sanitised

Recorded in the first real promotion round of the direct procedure, whose bind refused twice. `direct-return.json` is what the operator's direct `delegate_task` call returned: the bare task object, with no `structuredContent` and no `content` array. `thread-reads.json` holds `t3_thread_read` calls made through T3's direct tool on the same child after it completed: `fromStart` is the three reads bind makes (`afterPosition: -1`, then the original message's text from `textOffset` 2048 and 4096), and `laterMessage` the read after position 0, which gave the child's first assistant message. Each `args` is as sent; each response is stored as its page (`items`, `hasMore`, `nextPosition`) and the thread every one of them returned, stored once as `thread`. The reads that failed at bind were not recorded.

Identifiers and text are placeholders; times, statuses, the model and its options are as recorded. Each thread, task, node, run, item and message identifier keeps its recorded form with made-up UUIDs and native ids, consistent across both files, so parent, sender, child, task and run relate as recorded. The original message's text is the frozen task of the round `tests/catalog/t3-review-recorded-round.test.ts` captures (a made-up task with fixed nonce, request id and fetch time) after the review prefix, sliced at the recorded boundaries (2048, 2048 and 144 units); the assistant message's text is placeholder text. Only the fields the helper reads are kept, with the later message's recorded fields, whose missing `senderThreadId` is what makes it refused. When that round's capture changes, its first test fails showing the frozen task: slice the review prefix and it at 2048 and 4096 into the three `fromStart` pages. `tests/catalog/t3-code-mode-fixture.ts` serves both files (`recordedDirectReturn`, `recordedThreadRead`).
